question.text: Given the statement \[ P: \textrm{$2$ divides $8$} \] which of the following represents the statement $\neg P?$
question.explanation:
The symbol "$\neg$" represents negation. So, our task is to negate the given sentence.

To negate our plain English sentence, we place the words "It is not true that" in front of it. This gives the following:

\[ \neg P: \textrm{It is not true that $2$ divides $8$}, \]

In other words, $2$ does not divide $8.$ Therefore, $\neg P$ means the following:

\[ \neg P: \textrm{$2$ does } \textbf{not} \textrm{ divide $8$}. \]

Note that $P$ is true, while $\neg P$ is false.

question.text:
$10$ is not a prime number, and $0.1$ is a real number.

  • $P: \textrm{$10$ is a prime number}$

  • $Q: \textrm{$0.1$ is a real number}$
question.explanation:
The negation is represented by the symbol "$\neg$".

The sentence

$10$ is not a prime number

can be expressed symbolically as $\neg P.$

The sentence

$0.1$ is a real number

can be expressed symbolically as $Q.$

Therefore, the sentence

$10$ is not a prime number, and $0.1$ is a real number

can be expressed symbolically as $\neg P \land Q.$

question.text: Simplify the statement $ eg( eg P) \lor eg( eg (P \land Q)).$
question.explanation:
Two negations in a row cancel each other out. So:

  • we can simplify $\neg(\neg P)$ to $P,$ and

  • we can also simplify $\neg(\neg(P \land Q))$ to $P \land Q .$

Therefore, the given statement can be simplified to

\[ P \lor (P \land Q). \]

example.title: Simplifying a Double Negation

question.text: Simplify the statement $ eg[ eg ( eg B \lor eg ( eg A))].$
question.explanation:
Two negations in a row cancel each other out. So, we can simplify $\neg (\neg A)$ to $A.$

As a result of this, the statement simplifes to

\[ \neg[\neg (\neg B \lor A)] \]

Then, we can simplify $\neg (\neg (\neg B \lor A))$ to $\neg B \lor A.$

Therefore, the given statement can be simplified to

\[ \neg B \lor A. \]

question.text: Simplify the statement $ eg ( eg A) \land eg ( eg B).$
question.explanation:
Two negations in a row cancel each other out. So:

  • we can simplify $\neg (\neg A)$ to $A ,$ and

  • we can also simplify $\neg (\neg B)$ to $B.$

Therefore, the given statement can be simplified to

\[ A \land B. \]

question.text: Simplify the statement $ eg[ eg (A \land eg ( eg B))] \lor B.$
question.explanation:
Two negations in a row cancel each other out. So, we can simplify $\neg (\neg B)$ to $B.$

As a result of this, the statement simplifes to

\[ \neg (\neg (A \land B)) \lor B. \]

Then, we can simplify $\neg (\neg (A \land B))$ to $A \land B.$

Therefore, the given statement can be simplified to

\[ (A \land B) \lor B. \]
